title: Stelae of Aksum
summary: In the ancient Ethiopian capital Aksum, tall carved granite stelae were raised in the 3rd and 4th centuries CE to mark royal tombs. The largest, about 33 m long, lies where it fell while being erected. Stele 2, 21 m high, was taken to Rome in 1937 and re-erected in Aksum in 2008; a third still stands.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO's fact sheet gives the date of construction as the 3rd to 4th century AD, so the true start lies between 201 and 400. End is the present: the stelae field is still there.

phases.description: Stelae erected in the 3rd to 4th century AD as funerary markers; the Great Stele fell and shattered while being raised, in the 4th century.

Stele 3 stands and Stele 2 stands until it breaks; the Great Stele lies where it fell. The sources opened give no dated damage before 1937 (UNESCO says only that Stele 2 broke into five pieces near its original location).
Stele 2 was taken to Rome in 1937 and returned to Ethiopia in April 2005 in three blocks.
Stele 2 re-erected in Aksum in 2008 (UNESCO reinstallation project).

reviewer_note: Shape obelisk. The primary measured stele is Stele 2 (UNESCO gives height and base section); the Great Stele and Stele 3 figures are secondary and vary by source (Stele 3 is quoted from 21 to 24 m elsewhere; Stele 1 from 32.6 to 33 m). Least sure of the intact 400-1937 phase (bridged) and the 201 start (UNESCO says only 3rd-4th century).
